body.name: hoifHandle
body.construction:
Fix a number \(\gamma\) with \(d/(2t)<\gamma<1\), and fix an integer \(q\geq1\) such that \(q(1-\gamma)>1\).  Let \(\mathcal S_M\) be the space of periodic, cellwise tensor polynomials of coordinate degree at most \(p>\max\{\beta_e,\beta_m\}\) on a regular dyadic partition, and let \(z_M(x)\in\mathbb R^M\) be an \(L^2(dx)\)-orthonormal local basis of \(\mathcal S_M\), including the constant function.  Take the closest admissible dimension \(M=M_n\asymp n^\gamma\), and set the declared approximation rank to \(M_{\mathrm{proj}}=M\), so \(M_{\mathrm{proj}}=o(n)\).  Split the sample into two sets \(I,G\) of comparable sizes.  The following defines the directed estimator based on estimation set \(I\) and Gram set \(G\); the final estimator averages this construction with the roles of \(I,G\) reversed.

For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), put \(D_{a,i}=\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\), \(z_i=z_M(X_i)\),
\[
 \widehat\Omega_{a,G}=|G|^{-1}\sum_{i\in G}D_{a,i}z_i z_i^\top,
 \qquad
 \mathcal E_{a,G}=\left\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Omega_{a,G})\geq\frac{\eta c_X}{2},\ 
 \lambda_{\max}(\widehat\Omega_{a,G})\leq2C_X\right\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal E_{a,G}\), set \(B_{a,G}=\widehat\Omega_{a,G}^{-1}\) and
\[
 G_{a,i}=D_{a,i}z_i z_i^\top-\widehat\Omega_{a,G},
 \qquad R^p_{a,i}=D_{a,i}-1,
 \qquad R^\nu_{a,i}=D_{a,i}L_{Y_i}.
\]
For \(\ell\geq0\), define
\[
 A_{a,\ell}(i_1,\ldots,i_\ell)
 =B_{a,G}\prod_{u=1}^{\ell}(G_{a,i_u}B_{a,G}),
 \qquad A_{a,0}=B_{a,G}.
\]
For a displayed kernel whose indices are all distinct, let \(\mathbb{U}_I\) denote its ordered, without-replacement average over \(I\).  Define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C^{(1)}_{a,\ell}
 &=\mathbb{U}_I\!\left[
  (K_{X_{i_0}}\otimes R^\nu_{a,i_0})
  \{z_{i_0}^\top A_{a,\ell}(i_1,\ldots,i_\ell)z_{i_{\ell+1}}\}
  R^p_{a,i_{\ell+1}}
 \right],\\
 C^{(2)}_{a,\ell}
 &=\mathbb{U}_I\!\left[
  (K_{X_{i_0}}\otimes R^\nu_{a,i_{\ell+1}})
  R^p_{a,i_0}
  \{z_{i_0}^\top A_{a,\ell}(i_1,\ldots,i_\ell)z_{i_{\ell+1}}\}
 \right].
 \end{aligned}
\]
For \(0\leq\ell,r<q\), put \(j=\ell+r+2\) and define the two-branch term
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C^{(3)}_{a,\ell,r}=\mathbb{U}_I\!\Big[&
 D_{a,i_0}(K_{X_{i_0}}\otimes R^\nu_{a,i_j})
 \{z_{i_0}^\top A_{a,\ell}(i_1,\ldots,i_\ell)z_{i_{\ell+1}}\}
 R^p_{a,i_{\ell+1}}\\
 &\times
 \{z_{i_0}^\top A_{a,r}(i_{\ell+2},\ldots,i_{\ell+r+1})z_{i_j}\}
 \Big].
 \end{aligned}
\]
The arm correction and directed arm estimator are
\[
 \mathcal C_{a,q}^{I\mid G}
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^{q-1}(-1)^\ell\{C^{(1)}_{a,\ell}+C^{(2)}_{a,\ell}\}
 -\sum_{\ell,r=0}^{q-1}(-1)^{\ell+r}C^{(3)}_{a,\ell,r},
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_a^{I\mid G}
 =|I|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I}D_{a,i}K_{X_i}\otimes L_{Y_i}-\mathcal C_{a,q}^{I\mid G}.
\]
If either \(\mathcal E_{0,G}\) or \(\mathcal E_{1,G}\) fails, set the corresponding directed contrast to zero.  Otherwise set
\[
 \widehat\Psi^{I\mid G}=\widehat\theta_1^{I\mid G}-\widehat\theta_0^{I\mid G},
 \qquad
 \widehat\Psi_n^{\mathrm{ho}}=\frac12\left(\widehat\Psi^{I\mid G}+\widehat\Psi^{G\mid I}\right).
\]
For the finitely many \(n\) smaller than the largest displayed \(U\)-statistic order, take every unavailable correction to be zero.  Finally define the deterministic class constant
\[
 V_\star=1+\sup_{m\geq1}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
 mE_P\|\widehat\Psi_m^{\mathrm{ho}}-\Psi(P)\|_{\mathcal H}^2.
\]
The proof of the high-smoothness theorem shows \(V_\star<\infty\).  The associated test is the explicit sample map
\[
 \varphi_n^{\mathrm{ho}}
 =\mathbf 1\left\{\|\widehat\Psi_n^{\mathrm{ho}}\|_{\mathcal H}>sqrt{\frac{V_\star}{\alpha n}}\right\}.
\]
